dedupe_keys.name: nkom ros annual national risk and vulnerability assessments of the norwegian electronic communications sector

description: Nkom carries out annual national risk and threat assessments of Norway's electronic communications sector (Nkom ROS) and guides providers and users on risk and vulnerability in electronic communications. The Nkom ROS pages describe the framework and the analysis model Nkom uses to assess risk, with key concepts; experiences from past unwanted incidents, drawing mainly on providers' mandatory incident reporting to Nkom; societal, technological and threat trends; an overview and categorisation of the main risk areas in electronic communications as a starting point for others' own assessments; and example scenario analyses of risk areas carried out as part of Norway's national risk and preparedness work. The target group includes authorities, telecom actors and sectors that depend on electronic communications, such as municipalities, county authorities, county governors and private and public organisations. Coverage: Norway. Format and access: web pages and reports, free. Caveats: qualitative and semi-quantitative assessments; incident data behind them are not published in raw form; the report formats were not checked. Simulation uses: risk areas, scenarios and incident experience as structured inputs for telecom failure scenarios and for municipal risk assessments that depend on communications. Related records: the Nkom reinforced mobile coverage programme is one response to these risks, and the MIC Japan telecom accident statistics give comparable incident reporting.
